content.help: Off leaves the item menus of SkyUI exactly as they are and shows the pieces of hidden slots on your character while it stays off. The hidden slots are remembered and hide again when the panel is back on. Takes effect when the menu closes.

content.text: Sliders button in the bottom bar
content.help: The button in the bottom bar of the item menus that opens the sheet of settings. Off hides it, for a UI skin where it gets in the way. Everything on the sheet can still be set on these pages. Takes effect the next time a menu opens.

For mods that keep the world running while a menu is open, like Skyrim Souls RE. While the inventory is open, the pointer at an edge of the screen or a pushed stick no longer turns the camera behind the panel. Changes nothing when the game pauses in menus.

When you trade with a follower, the panel shows the follower: their doll, what they wear in the slots, and an item dragged into a slot goes on them. Works for any follower and any mod that opens a follower's inventory the game's way.

What you put on or take off a follower in the panel stays that way. The game doesn't swap it for gear it thinks is better, in a fight or out of it. A mod that changes a piece back 3 times within 10 minutes gets that piece. Off lets the game dress followers its own way.

Tabs over your character: YOU and each follower near you, nearest first. A click in your inventory opens that follower's trade, a click in a trade opens another follower's or your own inventory. They show only when a follower is near enough to be loaded. Takes effect the next time the menu opens.

Your character in the magic menu between the slots of your two hands and your voice, with the spell, weapon or shout each one holds. A click on a slot narrows the list to what can go there, and a spell picked then goes into that hand. A double click on a hand takes a weapon, shield or torch off. Takes effect the next time the menu opens.

Your character and your slots beside the list at a forge, a tanning rack, a workbench, a grindstone, an enchanter and the stations mods build on them. A right click on a piece of armor or a weapon tries it on for show, nothing is made or worn: the piece goes into its slot and on your character, and comes off by the same menu, by its slot or by trying another piece on the same slots. The companion tabs show a companion there to try pieces on them. All of it comes off as the menu closes. Takes effect the next time the menu opens. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

content.text: Let every follower be dressed again
content.help: A mod can ask the panel to leave a follower's gear as it is for a while, a quest's disguise say. If that mod is gone and a follower still can't be dressed in the panel, this lets every follower be dressed again.

How wide the panel of slots and your character is, in percent of all the room beside the item list. A narrower panel comes in from both sides and your character stays in the middle, for a UI skin or a screen where the slots lay over the rows. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar, where you see it change.

Moves a narrowed panel to the right, below zero to the left, in percent of all the room beside the item list. It moves only within that room, so a panel at full width stays put. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.
Your character in 3D between the two columns of slots, with everything you wear.

Standing: the character always stands calm and straight, even when you open the menu on a horse, sitting or mid swing. As in the world: the pose of the moment you opened the menu, with only the head and spine turned straight. In first person the character stands either way, the body plays a stance made for the camera there.
Drag across the character to turn it. Degrees it turns for every pixel the mouse moves.

With a mod of equipping animations, Immersive Equipping Animations and the like, the character plays the animation as you put a piece on or take it off. Once the inventory closes your character in the world plays it too, as without the panel.
The size of your character in percent of the size that fits between the slots. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar, where you see it change.
Moves your character to the right of the middle of its room, below zero to the left, in percent of the room's width.
Moves your character up from the middle of its room, below zero down, in percent of the room's height.

The colour of what is picked, lit or counted: the frame of a chosen slot, lit buttons and eyes, tabs, headings of the character drawer and the numbers beside slot names. Gold by default, pick one that sits with your UI. Takes effect the next time you open the menu.
The colour of names, signs and buttons at rest. Pale parchment by default. Takes effect the next time you open the menu.
Each slot shows the model of what you wear there. Off shows flat signs.

content.text: Armor as it sits on the body
content.help: Helmets, armor, gloves, boots, cloaks and jewelry are shown standing, the way they sit on you. Off shows the model the item has on the ground.

A small eye in the corner of a slot hides what you wear there on your character, in the world too. It stays worn and keeps protecting you. The eye of a small slot in a strip hides that piece alone. Hidden slots and pieces are saved with your game.

A click on a slot opens the window of what you wear there beside the slot, and selects it in the list when the list shows it. The list keeps its category, subcategories and search. A click anywhere else closes the window. Off only selects the item, a slot whose item the list doesn't show still opens its window.
A double click on a slot takes off what you wear there.
Drag a row of the list onto a slot or onto your character to put it on. A one handed weapon dropped on the left hand goes into the left hand.

A slot that holds more than one piece (a cloak, a bag and a lamp in Other, rings of several fingers) pulls out a strip of small slots when its tab is clicked: an empty one first that takes a dragged item, then one for every piece. Each can be opened, hidden, taken off or dropped on like a slot. Arrows and the wheel scroll a long strip, a click elsewhere, its handle or Esc put it back.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Off takes this slot off the panel, its place stays empty. What you wear there stays worn.
Every hidden slot and piece is shown on your character again.

Rows of the inventory, chests and shops show a picture of the item in place of its flat sign. The pictures are made once from the item's own model, as a save loads or when its row first shows, and kept as files. Off keeps the flat signs and makes none. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

How high the rows of the inventory, chests and shops are, in percent. The pictures grow with them and fewer rows fit on the screen. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar, where you see it change.

A green arrow and +N or a red arrow and -N after the name of an item you could wear: how much more or less armor or damage it gives than what you wear in its place. Ammo only counts while a bow or crossbow is in your hands, a bow is weighed against a bow and a sword against a melee weapon.
An item that gives exactly what you wear gets a grey equals sign instead of nothing.
A row of something you could wear shows the sign of the slot it goes to.

A strip under the category icons. Weapons: one handed, two handed, bows, staves, ammo. Apparel: light, heavy, clothing, jewelry, shields, and a second group head, body, hands, feet, other; two groups add up. Potions: health, magicka, stamina, poisons. Food and drinks. Books, notes, maps, spell tomes. Ore, ingots, gems, soul gems, pelts.
The name column gets a LAST ADDED state: what you got last comes first.
The weight column gets SUMW states: the weight of a whole stack instead of one item.
A small dot on what you got since you last closed the inventory, on its row and on its subcategory. It goes when the pointer passes the row or when the inventory closes.

A small arrowhead after the name of what a quest wants: gold while a quest still needs it, a dimmer gold when a quest that hasn't begun will, grey once its quest is done and you may let it go. The line of the item window that names the quest is Quest line on the Item window page. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

Stolen copies of an item get a row of their own beside the ones that are yours, in your inventory and in chests, so you see what is stolen and store, take, sell or drop just those. A merchant's or a follower's things stay as they are. Needs game 1.6 or later.

content.text: Right click opens the item menu
content.help: A right click on a row opens a small menu: equip, equip in the left hand, use, favorite, inspect, and drop, take, store, buy or sell one, all or some. Off gives the right click back to the game, which equips in the left hand.
In a container or a shop this key moves the whole stack of the row under the pointer at once, with no slider: take, store, buy or sell all of it.
In a chest or a shop the weight of a row turns red when taking one would slow you and amber when taking all of it would. The menu of a subcategory tells what it weighs.

The menu of a row or the junk key marks an item as junk, every copy of it. In a shop one press sells all your junk, in a chest it stores it. What you wear, your favorites and anything a quest wants are never taken.
Marks the row under the pointer as junk, or takes the mark off.

When the item window with its card comes up over the row under the pointer. On hover: at once. After a pause: once the pointer rests on a row a moment, so moving over the list shows nothing. UI's own card: no window over the rows, the card and the model of a row stay where SkyUI or your UI skin puts them, as without this mod, for a skin whose card stands apart; with plain SkyUI that place is over your character. A switch to it or from it comes with the next opening of the menu. In any of them Details in a row's right-click menu brings the window up and keeps it until you pick another row, and a click on a slot opens its window. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

The window of an item with its card, in percent. At 100 it takes about half the item list and never gets smaller than four tenths of the screen's height, so it reads on any screen. Make it bigger when the words of the card are too small for your screen, as on a TV across the room or a small handheld. It stops where the names of the rows would be covered. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

content.text: Card stays in the UI's place
content.help: The card of an item stays where and as SkyUI or your UI skin draws it, with the mod's numbers in it and the item's model beside it, and no window comes over the rows; Details in a row's right-click menu still brings the window up. Where the card lies over your character (plain SkyUI) it shows the way the item does with the character switched off. Window pops up set to the UI's own card goes first. It comes with the next opening of the menu. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

The item's name in the window, in percent of the size the card gives it. A name too long for its line at that size comes out as big as still fits. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

What a potion, an enchantment, a book or a spell does, as the card writes it, in percent. The card grows down and the numbers under it make room. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.
The combat numbers under the card, in percent. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

The kind under the name, what the item is made of in the corner of its picture and the small lines under the numbers: the quest, the body slots, how many you have, silver, the mod an item comes from and Stolen, in percent. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

Every word of SkyUI's card or your UI skin's card where the UI puts it, with the numbers the mod puts in it: on the right of the inventory when Card stays in the UI's place is on, and in a chest or a shop. In percent. The item window has its own four sizes above. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

Weapons show swing time, damage per second and per minute, reach, stagger and crit damage. Armor shows the share of a hit it stops, what the whole set stops and how much longer you last. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

A small tab at the feet of your character pulls your numbers up over it: level, health, magicka and stamina with how fast they come back, armor and resistances, swing time and damage a second of your weapon, speed, carry weight, what your gear weighs and how much of it slows you, sneak and power attacks, what enchantments and potions add to your skills, the spells in your hands, your bounties, and at the bottom the blessings, diseases and other effects on you. Click the tab or drag it as far as you like, the wheel scrolls. It stays out, the next time you open the menu too, until you push it back with the tab. Nothing is counted while it is in.

The window of anything you wear shows a small grey line with the body slots it takes, like Slots 32, 46. Handy with modular armor: pauldrons, belts and capes sit on slots 44 to 61, and two pieces on one slot push each other off. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

The kind under the name, like Heavy, Body, what the item is made of in the corner of its picture, and small grey lines under the numbers: how many you already have when it lies in a chest or a shop, silver, and the plugin it comes from when that is not the game itself. Quests have switches of their own, Quest line below and Mark quest items on the List page. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

A line under the numbers of what a quest wants: which quest, and whether it still needs the item or is done with it. The arrowhead after the name of the row is Mark quest items on the List page. With both off the mod reads nothing of the quests. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.

The quiet line From and the plugin's file under the numbers of an item a mod adds. Off hides just this line, the other quiet tags stay. Also set in the inventory with the sliders button in the bottom bar.
How long a swing takes to land, or a bow to draw. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
DPS, the damage of a weapon over a second of swings or shots. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
DPM, the same over a minute. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
How far a melee weapon reaches. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
How hard a hit staggers. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
The extra damage of a critical hit. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
The share of a hit a piece of armor stops, or would stop in place of what you wear. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
What all you wear stops together, and the game's cap. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
How much longer you last in a fight with the piece. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
Armor rating for each unit of weight. Off hides just this line of the combat numbers. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
The kind under the item's name, like Heavy, Body. One of the quiet tags. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.

A small list in the top left corner of the item's picture in the window, saying what the item is made of. Components: every part of the recipe that makes it at a forge or another bench, with how many it takes, like Iron Ingot (4), Leather Strips (3); an enchanted piece shows the recipe of the plain one it was made on. Material: only its material, like Steel Plate, as the item's keywords name it. An item no recipe makes (a unique one, loot, potions, books) shows its material when it has one, else nothing. The model of the item keeps clear of the list. One of the quiet tags. A card that stays in the UI's place has no window, so it has no list either, and a crafting station that writes what its recipe takes leaves the corner empty. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
You have 3, under the numbers of what lies in a chest or a shop. One of the quiet tags. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
Silver, under the numbers of a silver weapon. One of the quiet tags. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.
Stolen, or Stolen: 3 of 6, over the small lines. Also on the sliders sheet in the inventory, Item window page.

content.text: Zoom key opens the inspect view
content.help: The item zoom key of the game opens the full screen inspect view: drag to turn the item any way, the wheel brings it closer. Off leaves the game's own zoom.
